## Overview  

ImagineAI is a **browser‑based UI** for AI‑driven image generation. It showcases the **Next.js App Router** and leverages **Tailwind CSS** for a modern, responsive design while keeping the codebase **type‑safe** with TypeScript.

> **TL;DR** – Clone, install, run `npm run dev`, and start generating images locally.

Full autogenerated project details live in **[docs/README.generated.md](docs/README.generated.md)**.

---

## Features  

| ✅ | Feature |
|---|---|
| ✅ | **Prompt editor** with live validation |
| ✅ | **Image preview grid** with lazy loading |
| ✅ | **Responsive layout** (mobile‑first) |
| ✅ | **API abstraction** in `lib/` for swapping AI providers |
| ✅ | **Dark / light theme** toggle (Tailwind + CSS variables) |
| ✅ | **Type‑safe** interfaces in `types/` |
| ✅ | **Server‑side rendering** for SEO‑friendly share links |
| ✅ | **Extensible component library** in `components/` |
| ✅ | **Environment‑configurable** via `.env.local` |

A deeper technical dive is available in **[docs/TECHNICAL_OVERVIEW.md](docs/TECHNICAL_OVERVIEW.md)**.

## Tech Stack  

| Layer | Tool | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **Framework** | Next.js (App Router) | File‑system routing, SSR, API routes |
| **UI** | React 18 + Tailwind CSS | Component‑driven UI, utility‑first styling |
| **Language** | TypeScript 5 | Compile‑time safety |
| **Package Manager** | npm (works with pnpm) | Widely supported |
| **Bundler** | built‑in Next.js (Webpack/ Turbopack) | Zero‑config defaults |
| **Version Control** | Git (GitHub) | Collaboration & CI pipelines |

## Setup  

```bash
# 1️⃣ Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/anubhabx/ImagineAI.git
cd ImagineAI

# 2️⃣ Install dependencies (npm or pnpm)
npm ci          # or: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

# 3️⃣ Create a .env.local file (copy the example)
cp .env.example .env.local
# Edit .env.local with your AI provider credentials

# 4️⃣ Run the development server
npm run dev   # → http://localhost:3000
```

The app will auto‑reload on file changes.

---

## Scripts  

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Start Next.js in development mode (hot‑reloading) |
| `npm run build` | Produce an optimized production build (`.next`) |
| `npm start` | Run the production build locally (`NODE_ENV=production`) |
| `npm run lint` | Run ESLint against `src/**/*.tsx` |
| `npm run format` | Run Prettier (code formatting) |
| `npm run type-check` | Execute `tsc --noEmit` for pure type validation |
| `npm run clean` | Delete `.next`, `node_modules`, and lockfiles (useful for CI) |

All scripts are defined in `package.json`; feel free to extend them.

## Testing  

The repository does **not** ship a test suite yet. To add one:

1. Install a test runner (e.g., Jest + React Testing Library):  

   ```bash
   npm i -D jest @types/jest ts-jest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom
   ```

2. Add a `jest.config.ts` file and place tests under `__tests__/` or `*.test.tsx`.  

3. Create a script:  

   ```json
   "test": "jest"
   ```

4. Run `npm test`.

> **Future work:** CI pipelines (GitHub Actions) will automatically run linting, type‑checking, and tests on PRs.

## Deployment  

### Vercel (recommended)

1. **Push** your code to the `master` branch.  
2. In the Vercel dashboard, **Import** the GitHub repository.  
3. Vercel auto‑detects the Next.js app, installs dependencies, runs `npm run build`, and deploys.  

#### Environment Variables

Add the variables from `.env.example` to Vercel’s **Project Settings → Environment Variables** (Production, Preview, Development).

### Other Platforms  

| Platform | Steps |
|---|---|
| **Docker** | `docker build -t imagineai . && docker run -p 3000:3000 imagineai` |
| **Node.js server** | `npm run build && npm start` (serve on any host) |
| **Static export** (no server‑side features) | `npm run export` → `out/` folder, then host on any static CDN |

## Contributing  

We welcome contributions! Follow these steps:

1. **Fork** the repository.  
2. **Create** a feature branch: `git checkout -b feature/awesome‑thing`.  
3. **Commit** with a clear message: `git commit -m "feat: add awesome thing"`.  
4. **Push** and open a **Pull Request** against `master`.  
5. Ensure **lint**, **type‑check**, and (if present) **tests** pass.  

Read the full contribution guide in **[CONTRIBUTING.md]** (if added) or refer to the autogenerated docs.

### Code Style  

| Rule | Tool |
|---|---|
| **Formatting** | Prettier (`npm run format`) |
| **Linting** | ESLint (`npm run lint`) |
| **Types** | TypeScript (`npm run type-check`) |

All new files should reside under the appropriate folder (`components/`, `lib/`, `types/`, etc.) and include JSDoc/TS doc comments where useful.
